title: Reproduce the real workflow, including the umask
explanation: `sudo -u dataexport sh -c "umask 027; touch /srv/exports/probe"` succeeds (dataexport owns the directory, so writing was never the issue), but `sudo -u analyst test -r /srv/exports/probe` is denied — even though analyst is a member of `exportreaders`, the group that owns the directory.

title: Check what group the new file actually landed in
explanation: `ls -l /srv/exports/probe` shows a group other than `exportreaders` — one only `dataexport` belongs to. `ls -ld /srv/exports` confirms there's no setgid bit, so this directory does nothing to force new files to inherit its own group; whatever group a file gets comes entirely from the process that created it.

title: New-file group assignment reads the primary group, never the supplementary list
explanation: `id dataexport` shows its primary group is its own private group, not `exportreaders` — even though the account could theoretically be added to `exportreaders` as a supplementary group. The kernel assigns a newly created file's group from the creating process's effective/primary GID; supplementary groups are consulted only when checking permissions against files that already exist, never when deciding what group a brand-new file gets.

title: usermod -g, not -aG — the two solve different problems
explanation: `usermod -aG exportreaders dataexport` would make dataexport a member of the group and even let it read/write existing exportreaders-owned files, but it would not change what group future files it creates come out as, since that decision reads the primary GID field. Only `sudo usermod -g exportreaders dataexport` changes the value the kernel actually consults at file-creation time.

title: Verify with a fresh file, not the one from step 1
explanation: Re-running the same umask-027 probe against a new filename and testing `analyst`'s read access confirms the fix changes behavior for files created *from now on* — the earlier probe file, created before the fix, would stay group-owned however it already was and isn't a valid check on its own.
